connections.why: Both are foundation approaches offering contrasting explanations of behaviour
Cognitive processes ultimately depend on the underlying biology of the brain
Biological and learning approaches debate how far behaviour is innate or learned
Conditioning principles explain how addictive behaviours are acquired
Biological explanations underpin the dopamine model of schizophrenia
Cognitive theory underlies work on eyewitness memory and reliability
Social explanations help account for offending behaviour
Social learning theory explains how criminal behaviour can be modelled
Biological maturation links to attachment and atypical development
Diagnostic systems are applied when classifying schizophrenia
The same classification framework is used for the second disorder
Foundation studies are evaluated through their research methods
Sound study design is needed before data can be meaningfully analysed
Research-methods knowledge is applied to evaluate the reliability of diagnosis
Statistical understanding supports the evaluation of key studies
Foundation topics provide the material for debates on ethics and culture
Clinical topics such as schizophrenia raise issues of ethics and social control
Classic studies from the foundation topics are reviewed synoptically
Methodological issues feed directly into wider debates about the discipline
